title: Should we pay more for chocolate?

vocabulary.meaning: the powder or raw material made from cacao beans and used to make chocolate
examples: Cocoa prices have risen sharply.
Many farmers depend on cocoa production.

vocabulary.meaning: a person who grows cacao trees for cocoa beans
examples: Cocoa farmers often receive only a small share of the final chocolate price.
Fairer prices can improve cocoa farmers' incomes.

vocabulary.meaning: a system intended to give producers in poorer countries better prices and working conditions
examples: She buys fair-trade chocolate when possible.
Fair trade aims to support small farmers.

vocabulary.meaning: the stages involved in producing and delivering a product
examples: Chocolate has a long global supply chain.
Companies are under pressure to make their supply chains more transparent.

vocabulary.meaning: enough income to provide a decent standard of living for a household
examples: Many farmers do not earn a living income.
Higher cocoa prices could support a living income.

vocabulary.meaning: buying products in ways that consider workers, animals, and the environment
examples: Ethical consumption can influence company behaviour.
Some consumers are willing to pay more for ethically produced food.

vocabulary.meaning: an extra amount paid above the usual price
examples: Fair-trade farmers may receive a premium.
Consumers sometimes pay a premium for sustainable products.

vocabulary.meaning: official confirmation that a product or process meets certain standards
examples: The chocolate carries an ethical certification label.
Certification can help consumers identify responsible products.

vocabulary.meaning: the circumstances in which people work, including pay, safety, and hours
examples: Campaigners want better labour conditions on cocoa farms.
Consumers increasingly ask about labour conditions.

vocabulary.meaning: buying raw materials in ways that can continue without serious social or environmental harm
examples: The company promised more sustainable sourcing of cocoa.
Sustainable sourcing requires cooperation across the supply chain.
